translation:
Dispelling the Darkness of Mind.
Instruction on Taking Refuge, the Foundation of All the Paths of All the Buddhist Practitioners.
The three excellences of the outer refuge are lifted like a crown.
The three roots of the inner refuge are directly accomplished.
The three kayas of actual refuge are actualized.
I prostrate at the feet of the peerless teacher.

The first is the foundation of all paths, an instruction on taking refuge that is explained in the four summarized topics: the classification of taking refuge, the way of taking refuge, revealing advice, and the benefits.

1. The first topic, [classification of refuge]. [~]
Generally, taking refuge is the door opener to all the dharmas.
The door opener of taking refuge is confidence. Initially, in taking refuge, it is important to raise steady confidence.
Confidence is divided into three classes: lucid confidence, aspiring confidence, and trusting confidence - the three are present.

1.1. [Lucid confidence] [~] First, lucid confidence is [when] visiting a temple where symbolic objects representing the buddha's body, speech, and mind exist, or by personally meeting gurus, spiritual friends, and superior beings, or
Generating confidence in mind by drawing a pure aspiration after hearing their life stories and qualities and thinking that their kindness to me is immense is referred to as lucid confidence.

1.2. Aspiring confidence [~]
After hearing about the sufferings of cyclic existence of the three bad migrations and so on, the desire to be separated from it arises.
Not having confidence in the higher level gods, when hearing about the happiness of emancipation, the desire to attain it arises.
Hearing the benefits of virtues arises a desire to accomplish them while seeing the flaws of negative actions arises a desire to abandon them.

1.3. [Trusting confidence]  [~]
After knowing about the extraordinary blessings and qualities of the three precious jewels, in sadness, happiness, illness, death, life, or with whatever karma occurred, one thinks of the non-deceptive refuge, the three jewels.
One thinks that there is no trust or hope in others, this is trusting confidence.
Padmasambhava says:
There is a blessing through trusting confidence.
If the rational mind is free from doubts, whatever you think will be accomplished.
Thus, it was said as above.
Therefore, confidence is like a seed that gives birth to all the good qualities of white dharmas. The absence of confidence is like the seed burned by fire.
From Sutra:
For the people without confidence
The white dharma won’t occur.
Similar to the seed burned by fire,
It won’t give birth to the blue-green sprouts.

It was said so.
So confidence is the main of the seven riches of the noble ones.

The precious wheel of confidence
Connects to the path of virtue day and night.

As it is said, it is the best of all riches, and likewise, it is a treasure because it is the source of inexhaustible good qualities. It is like the feet for walking onto the path of emancipation. It is like the hand that gathers all the virtuous dharmas into one’s continuum.

Confidence is the best of wealth, treasures, and feet.
Similar to a hand, confidence is the root of gathering virtues.
It was said so.
Thus, even though the three jewels have inconceivable compassion and blessings, for them to enter one’s own continuum, confidence and devotion are very important.
If you have excellent confidence and devotion, excellent compassion and blessings will come from the guru and the three jewels.
For the medium one, medium. For the little one, little. If there is no confidence and devotion at all, compassion and blessings will be absent.

For example, even though the monk Sunakshatra stayed as the assistant of Buddha for twenty-five years, he had wrong views and did not have any confidence. In the end, he was like a hungry ghost born in the garden of flowers.

One who has no confidence even when Buddha arrives in front [of them]. 
One who has no compassion even when animal intestines are being pulled down.
If these two are absent, how could blessings take place? [~]
It was said like that.
If you have confidence and devotion from the core of your heart, then the complete Buddha himself will reside in their presence and will transform into a blessing.
As it is said:
Whoever has devotion and mental attention,
In front of him, Buddha resides,
And [he] is blessed by bestowing empowerment.
And also by Padmasambhava:
Man or woman having confidence
Has Padmasambhava near his door without going anywhere.
In my life, death does not exist.
There is one Padmasambhava in front of each person having confidence.
If you have trusting confidence, the compassion of Buddha will have a place anywhere.
It is said that by having confidence, the old lady will see Buddha through the dog’s tooth.
In the past, there was an old lady and her son.
The son travelled to India frequently for trade.
“Son, I, old woman, request you.
Bodhgaya, the holy place of the noble land of India, is the place that many buddhas have visited. Therefore,
can you bring for me a special object for prostration from India?”
Even though being asked for this many times, the son forgot to take an object.
When the son was going for a trade to India again:
“If this time you do not carry for me the special object for prostration, I will kill myself in front of you.”
The son went to India, and after finishing trading, returned again forgetting about it.
After arriving at the house, he remembered what his mother had said.
“What should I do now? I haven’t taken the special object for prostration for my old mother.”
Thinking that now his old mother would kill herself by jumping from height,
he looked around and saw a dog’s head at some corner.
He pulled out its tooth, wrapped it with silk, and carrying it, went to the mother.
“This is the canine tooth of Buddha for you, mother, so make it into an object for your supplication!”

The mother truly cherished the dog's tooth as Buddha's tooth and she aroused confidence [in it]. During that time, she continuously did prostrations and offerings, and because of that, many relics came out of the dog's tooth.
At the time of the old lady’s death, a pavilion of rainbow light and so on occurred.

Even though there is no blessing from the dog's tooth, by the power of the great confidence of the old lady, the blessings of Buddha were put into the dog’s tooth. So there was no difference between it and Buddha’s tooth.
Not only that, direct realization of the truth of the true meaning of reality depends exclusively on confidence.
Also from Sutra:

Shariputra, it is through confidence that superfactual [truth] is realized. [~]
It was said.

By the power of arising extraordinary confidence, the blessings of the guru and the three jewels enter into one’s continuum. Therefore, perfect realization arises within. When one sees the meaning of the true reality, [he] trusts in the guru and the three jewels.
By arising extraordinary infallible confidence, the realization of reality and trusting confidence help each other.

In the past, when precious Dagpopa was leaving, Jetsun Milarepa asked him when he was going to maintain the gathering.
Asking that:
“When the essence of mind, different from now, comes into full view, and realization of special insight is born within.

At that time, even I, an old man, arise steady confidence in actually seeing Buddha. Therefore, at that time, [I] will maintain the gathering.”
It was said.
In this way, through extraordinary confidence and devotion, the unchanging mind of complete trust is indispensable, as it is like the opening door to taking refuge.
Taking refuge, which has that kind of confidence, has three types in terms of motivation.
According to that, hell, hungry ghosts, and animal realms,
if after being horrified by the sufferings of the three lower realms, one takes refuge to find the ease of higher-level gods and humans, it is known as the taking refuge of a lesser person.
Knowing that wherever one is born, in higher or lower realms of samsara, he is not beyond the intrinsic nature of suffering.
Merely seeking the peace of nirvana to become liberated from the sufferings of samsara, if one then takes refuge in the three jewels, it is known as the taking refuge of a middling person.
After seeing that all these sentient beings which exist in this limitless samsara, the ocean of suffering, are tormented by inconceivably many sufferings,
one then takes refuge for the sake of setting them in a rank of truly complete buddha. It is known as taking refuge of the great person.
In this way, out of the three motivations, in case one desires to set infinite sentient beings in a state of complete buddha, he needs to take refuge of the great person.

Even though the mere bliss of the higher realms such as gods and humans, appear to be temporary happiness, in reality they are not beyond suffering. Once the pleasurable results of higher realms are exhausted, one will fall again into the lower realms. Therefore,
seeking the ease of the higher realms only for a brief moment has no purpose.

Even if you alone attain peaceful and full of ease nirvana, state of shravaka and pratyekabuddha, it is not acceptable that you do not do anything for the sake of all the sentient beings that are your fathers and mothers, who fell into the limitless ocean of suffering since the beginningless time.
The path of a great person is taking refuge due to wanting all the sentient beings to attain state of buddha. It is the entrance to immeasurable merit and should be attended by such a person.
From Precious Garland:
To the immeasurable realm of sentient beings,
Likewise, there is the desire to benefit [them].
It was said so.

2. [The way of taking refuge] [~]
In the way of taking refuge, there are ten summarazed meanings -

basis of characterization, characteristics, classification, difference, essence, difference between the resultant refuge and aspiring mind, purpose, meaning of the term, the ultimate object of refuge, and the way of meditation.
2.1. Basis of characterization.
Perfected in both abandonment and realization, and endowed with two purposes, for oneself and others, is the complete buddha.
Peaceful, free from desire is the holy dharma.
Having both intelligence and liberation is the noble sangha. These are the three jewels.
2.2. Characteristics.
The buddha jewel, the embodiment of four kayas and five exalted wisdoms, who is endowed with the two-fold purity, two ultimate purposes, and eight perfect characteristics.
By Maitreya:
Uncompounded, spontaneous attainment,
[These two qualities] cannot be realized [completely] by other conditions.
Having [exalted] knowledge, [great] love, and power,
Buddha is the only one who has two purposes.
It was said so.

The subjects of dharma are the uncontaminated immaculate truths, encompassed by cessation and path. The means of expression is the perfect speech that appears in names, words, and letters. Thus, the scriptural and realized dharmas are endowed with the eight characteristics.
Inconceivable, non-dual, non-conceptual,
Pure, clear, has the remedy aspect,
The truth of cessation, the truth of the path, freedom from desire,
Has the characteristics of the two truths, that is the dharma.
It was said so.
The actual sangha is the one endowed with the qualities of wisdom and liberation of bodhisattvas, the victor's sons, of the great ground.
By Guardian Maitreya:

Having knowledge of how it is and knowledge of the extent,
The inner wisdom, pure observation,
[They] are intelligent, have a gathering of irreversibility,
And possess the highest qualities.
It was said so.

2.3. [Classification] [~]
Classification - common and uncommon.

2.4. [Difference] [~] 
The difference - the place of refuge, time, cause, for whom it is done.
2.4.1. The place of refuge.
All the shravakas that take resultant refuge are arhats.
Those who, after abandoning suffering and listening to the dharma in the presence of Buddha, explain it to others are considered to be the sangha jewel.

All the solitary realizers meditate on twelve links of dependent-origination in forward and reverse orders. They realize all the profound dharmas of dependent-origination. Therefore it is considered that the dharma jewel expels suffering.
The Mahayana practitioners take refuge in the Lord Buddha as being free from perishing or destruction.
The places of causal refuge, all three of them - one adheres to Buddha as the teacher, dharma as the path, and sangha as the friends.

2.4.2. [Time] [~]
The time - by the Hinayana practitioners - for as long as one lives,
by the Mahayana practitioners - until enlightenment.

2.4.3. Cause. [~]
The Hinayana practitioners take refuge with confidence because they themselves desire to be freed from the sufferings. The Mahayana practitioners take refuge based on great compassion for the sake of the liberation of all the sentient beings from suffering.

2.4.4. For whom it is done. [~]
The Hinayana practitioners do it for themselves. The Mahayana practitioners take refuge for the sake of others to be liberated from the sufferings.
Here taking refuge, which has four special qualities, is considered to be extraordinary.

2.5. Essence. [~]
By seeking the result, a place without fear, Buddha, one accepts Buddha as the teacher, dharma as the path, and sangha as the friend - this is the essence of taking refuge.

And if by seeking for that result, together with the teacher, complete Buddha, one holds on to Brahma, Ishvara, Vishnu, and others, one seeks for the lower results, and this is not an excellent way of taking refuge.

2.6. [Difference between resultant refuge and aspiring mind] [~]
What is the difference between resultant refuge and arousing of aspiring mind? Just seeking enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings is taking refuge,
that very thought of acting under the power of the iron hook of the vow is arousing of aspiring mind.
2.7. Purpose.
[The purpose is] to differentiate between buddhist practitioners and outsiders, and to produce vows for laypersons, novices, monks, and so on.

It has great protection from negative influences, obstructors, and others. It reduces karmic obscurations of wrong devotion. It includes one among superior ones. It is expressed for gods and nagas who have confidence in the teaching.

2.8. Meaning of the term. [~]
From the Sanskrit term “ratna” comes the term precious. Because of having the six qualities in accordance with dharma, it is defined as a jewel.
From the Sublime Continuum:
Because of being of rare appearance, because of being stainless,
Because of being powerful, and because of
Being an ornament of the world, and because of having excellence,
Because of being changeless, it is the jewel.
It was said so.
Being of rare appearance is in accordance with dharma; even though the world changes throughout eons, sentient beings do not meet the dharma and do not produce the root of virtue.
Being stainless is in accordance with dharma; it is apart from everything which has a stain of fault.
Being powerful is in accordance with dharma; having inconceivable power of the qualities of the six super-knowledges and such, it dispels troubles of the world.
To be an ornament of the world is in accordance with dharma; good actions of all beings are caused by it.
Out of artificial jewels, having excellence is in accordance with dharma; it possesses transcendental good qualities.
Being changeless under any conditions like praise and blame, and so on, is in accordance with dharma because of being the intrinsic nature of uncompounded dharmata.

2.9. The ultimate object of refuge. [~]
The ultimate object of refuge is exclusively Buddha and not the other two. It is so because if one sees the truth, he should abandon all the scriptural dharma. Tantric realizations are continuously developing in boddhisattvas, Hinayana practitioners, and solitary realizers and therefore are not permanent, and are deceptive. All the sangha members themselves are still traveling on the path. They have fear as they do not rely on Buddha. They have no power to abandon latent tendencies and all the obscurations of their own state, that is why they are not ultimate.
From the Sublime Continuum:
As being abandoned, as a deceptive subject,
As being nonexistent, and as endowed with fear -
The two dharmas and the assembly of sangha
Are not the ultimate supreme refuge.
Following the superfactual [truth],
Buddha is the only refuge.
It was said so.

2.10. The way of meditation. [~]
Always while walking, from the state of mind not separated from mindfulness and alertness, in the space above the right shoulder, cultivate the three refuges and an assembly of deities.
That is the place of circumambulation.
At the time of sitting, meditate on the space above the crown of the head.
That is the support for supplication.
While eating and drinking, meditate on the center of the throat.
That is the area of offering a select portion of whatever is being eaten and being drunk.
At the time of falling asleep, meditate on the heart center.
That is the hidden main point for transforming confusion into luminosity.

In this way, in all one's conduct, without separating the clear appearance of the objects of refuge, it is very important that taking refuge must be performed while putting trust in the three jewels through the confidence of total reliance.

3. [Explanation of instruction] [~]
Explanation of instruction has four parts; instruction on prostration, instruction on what is to be abandoned, instruction on what will be accomplished, and appropriate instruction.

3.1. [Instruction on prostration.] [~]
At the time of prostration, one prostrates through the body, takes refuge, and recites words of whatever prayer is known through the speech. No matter what is performed by the mind, it is important that you should keep your awareness with steady confidence and dedication.
This way, the three doors are focused all together, and one should visualize self and all the sentient beings doing prostrations together, and so on. This is an important point.
If this is not done, the distracted mind will follow along after outer objects.
If it happens that someone is sitting, walking, or talking on the right side, and your eyes and awareness become distracted towards that side, place the palms on the left cheek.
The same way [should be performed] for the left side.
If the mind falls under the control of complete distraction,
only the body pretends to prostrate while [performing] body movement. This does not have any essence and is the cause of great weariness.
By Kyobpa Jigten Sumgon:
The guru, one's own mind, and Buddha, the three,
For a yogi, who realizes that they are one,
There is no need to arise fabricated devotion.
It was said like this.

Furthermore, when one prostrates, one should join palms together hollowly, like an opening lotus. If there is no empty space between palms and two palms meet, that is the hand posture of the Tirthika followers.
If only the tips of the fingers meet, it is the prostration of the clueless fool. Both are improper.
From the Sutra of Great Emancipation Extending Throughout the Ten Directions:
Similar to the lotus’s opening buds,
Two hands at the crown, placing the palms together.
The body is associated with the unfathomable gathering of clouds.
Prostrate to the buddhas of ten directions.
It was said so.
Then gradually, the obscurations of the body are cleansed by placing the palms on the crown,
the obscurations of the speech are cleansed by placing the palms at the throat,
the obscurations of the mind are cleansed by placing the palms at the heart center.

The forehead, palms, and knees, the so-called five principal parts of the body should touch the ground during prostration. The obscurations of afflictions of the five poisons are cleansed by bringing all five down to the ground during prostration.
For the purpose of obtaining blessings from the body, speech, mind, good qualities, enlightened activities, and so on, [one] will do it this way.
Then again, one should stand up and straighten the spine, then join the palms, and do the prostration as before.

3.2. The three things to be abandoned. [~]
Do not prostrate to the samsaric gods while prostrating to Buddha.
Non-buddhist gods such as Shiva, Vishnu, and others, have not liberated themselves from the sufferings of samsara.
Furthermore, when seeking refuge for the next life, one should never prostrate and make offerings to powerful worldly gods and demons such as local deities, earth lords, and so on.
After taking refuge in dharma, abandon being harmful to other sentient beings.
By making intense effort, try your best not to do any action of harming other sentient beings even during dreams.
After taking refuge in the sangha, do not keep company with Tirthika followers,
One should avoid associating with those who, like Tirthika followers, criticize and disparage your guru and dharma and deprecate the profound dharma of the tantric teachings.
3.3. Three accomplishments.
After taking refuge in Buddha, make an offering with respect to the image of Buddha jewel above, even if it is broken.
Hold it up by the crown of the head and put it in a clean place.
Direct perception of Buddha jewel is generated, which leads to maintaining confidence and pure perception.
After taking refuge in the dharma, the respect for even the excellent speech letters Ka, Kha is generated.

Hold it up by the crown of the head and consider the dharma as an actual jewel. After taking refuge in the sangha, sangha is a jewel. Consider sangha with an orange patch symbol as an actual jewel, and make an offering with respect.
Make an offering by the crown of the head, put it in a clean place, and maintain confidence and pure perception.

Especially in the Vajrayana of the Secret Mantra, the main object of refuge is the guru. The body of the guru is sangha, the speech of the guru is dharma, and the mind of the guru is Buddha. He is known to be the essential embodiment of the three jewels. Therefore, see whatever he does as good and attend to him with a fixated, changeless awareness. First thing in the morning, you should always offer three or seven prostrations and repeat the words of taking refuge. You should do it the same way in the evening.
I take refuge in guru.
I take refuge in Buddha.
I take refuge in dharma.
I take refuge in sangha.
I take refuge in the gathering of heroes, dakinis, dharma-protectors, and guards - everyone that possesses the wisdom eye.
In Buddha, dharma, and sangha,
Until I am enlightened, I take refuge.
Through the merit of practicing generosity and other good deeds,
May I attain buddhahood for the sake of sentient beings.
Perform this. It is known as a fourfold taking refuge in the yidam.
3.4. Three appropriate [instructions].

Now consider the guru, the spiritual friend, teaching you the state of acceptance and rejection, as an actual Buddha jewel. Do not even step over the shadow of his body, and make an effort to offer your service and honour.

Whatever instruction is granted by the speech of the pure guru should be considered as the actual dharma jewel. Therefore, whatever is spoken should be earnestly accepted and shouldn't be disobeyed even slightly.

The followers and disciples of the guru, your friends, who behave similarly to brahmins, should be considered as the actual sangha jewel. Respect them through the body, speech, and mind. Do not make them displeased even for just a moment.

There was nothing that Jowo Je, the glorious Atisha, did not know or see from an ocean of the teachings of sutra and tantra. However, he said that taking refuge was the most important thing at the beginning and explained refuge. Thus, he was known as the refuge Pandita.
Once a Buddhist practitioner enters into the path of emancipation, taking refuge and instruction on taking refuge should be practiced without abandonment, even at the cost of one's life.
From Sutra:
The one who is taking refuge in Buddha
Is a genuine lay practitioner,
In the other deities
He has never taken refuge.
Taking refuge in dharma
Is freedom from the harmful mind.
Taking refuge in noble sangha
Means not being friends with Tirthika followers.
It was said like this.
4. Benefits of taking refuge.
By just taking refuge, the seed of emancipation is planted,
oneself is distanced from the collections of non-virtues,
and virtue increases.
[Taking refuge] becomes the basis of all the vows and the source of all the good qualities.
Temporary benefits are that one is protected by the virtuous gods, one’s wishes are accomplished, and so on.
And finally, one attains buddhahood. It is said that there are unfathomable benefits.
From Condensed Prajnaparamita in Verse:
If the merit of taking refuge has a form,
Even the three realms are small vessels for it.
The ocean is a treasury of water.
How can the handful measure it?
It was said so.
King Ajatashatru took refuge after killing his father. He experienced hell for seven days, and it is said that because of having taken refuge, he was freed after seven days.
Like Devadatta, who committed three immediate heinous karmas and [gained] trust in Buddha's speech while being burned alive in hell [and said]:
“Now I take refuge in Buddha from the depth of my bones”.
After saying that, he became a solitary buddha known as Devadatta.
Since it has such immeasurable benefits, this place of refuge, the basis of all Dharma, should be practiced assiduously by all boys and girls, young and old, great and small.
Despite relying on the three refuges, heart-felt trust is limited,
Even after taking the three trainings, abiding and respecting vows will fade away like a rainbow.
Bless me and other foolish sentient beings, similar to me,
To have steady, irreversible confidence.

This is compiled by His Eminence Togtrul Thupten Tenpei Gyaltsen on the request for the teaching of taking refuge, the root of the dharma, by the Phyang Youth Association with auspicious offerings on the third day of the Miracle month of the Water-Pig year of Mangyul, in February 1983, at Tendrelling, the private residence in Leh. MANGALAM
